name: cited_oracle_inputs: weather entry with quantized fractional temp_f (ADR_019)
__comment: ADR_019 (forbid-floats + Wave-4 observation quantization) supersedes the
prior float form of this vector. canonicalize now REJECTS non-integer
numbers, so a raw float temp_f (75.2) can no longer reach value_hash. The
producer quantizes temp_f through the ONE shared quantizer
quantize temp_f -> { value_int: round(75.2 * 1000), scale: 1000, unit: 'millidegf' }
The preimage is now FLOAT-FREE, so sraid canonicalize and the conformance
local jcs() produce byte-identical output (cross-language conformant):
This vector proves the quantized (ADR_019-conformant) fractional shape;
valid.json weather entry (temp_f: 78, an integer) still covers the integer
case unchanged, because integer readings pass through the quantizer as-is.
notes: raw_value.temp_f is the ADR_019 quantized shape { value_int, scale, unit }: proves fractional temps are float-free before hashing.
Source Celsius: 24.0 C. Fahrenheit: Math.round((24.0 * 9/5 + 32) * 10) / 10 = 75.2, quantized at scale 1000 (millidegf) to value_int 75200.
value_int, scale are integers and unit is a string, so canonicalize does not throw (ADR_019 forbid-floats); a raw float temp_f (75.2) would still be rejected.
sraid canonicalize and the suite local jcs() emit identical bytes for this preimage; value_hash = sha256(JCS(raw_value)).
Complement to valid.json weather entry (temp_f: 78) which covers the integer-valued case (passes through the quantizer unchanged).
feed_claimed_at is omitted; absence (not null) per spec Section 1.3 rule 3.
